A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SELF-REDTEAM work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original safety, capability, diversity and ablation results, including additional model families and multi-turn evaluation in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 reports original training and evaluation results, including safeguarding comparisons, computational measurements and attack-novelty analyses.

M1.justification: The shared attacker-defender policy, hidden CoT, reward components, role-specific advantage normalization, Re++ objective and auxiliary SFT remain unchanged. The revised Algorithm 1 makes mixed-role batching explicit without establishing a different training procedure.

E1.justification: BBH-CoT, evaluated in v2 Table 2 and described in Appendix C.2, is omitted from v3. The remaining training and evaluation coverage is retained. StrongREJECT and multi-turn X-Teaming already appeared in v2 Appendix A; their prominence in v3 does not constitute new coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix D.2 adds evaluated LLM-LAT and CircuitBreaker comparisons on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Tables 12–13). This substantially extends comparisons beyond the initial models and internal role, CoT and SFT variants evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: v3 extends general-capability evaluation configurations to trained variants of three Qwen sizes and standard Llama (Tables 8–11), and introduces controlled runtime comparisons and base-model-perplexity evaluation. Appendix A.2 also specifies stopping at 200 steps within the retained 300-step learning-rate schedule. These changes do not establish that every earlier experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 measures self-play's computational overhead, while D.4 tests attack novelty through diversity and perplexity relative to the initial attacker. Capability ablations are also expanded across model configurations. Multi-turn transfer, hidden-CoT ablations and emergent attacker refusals were already investigated in v2.

E5.justification: Figure 3 changes from means over eight runs to three runs, retaining 95% confidence intervals. v3 newly states that Table 1 and ablations average at least three independent trials. The earlier eight-checkpoint bootstrap distributions and refusal-case statistics remain; there is no basis for claiming an overall increase in runs.

E6.justification: Many preliminary scores are revised. For Qwen2.5-14B Self-play + SFT, WJB harmful ASR changes from 0.419 to 0.372 and AlpacaEval from 36.58 to 38.088; Defender-only + SFT changes from 38.24 to 35.500, reversing their AlpacaEval ordering (v2 Table 5; v3 Table 2). These are revised estimates, not established same-setting gains. New capability, safeguarding, runtime and novelty results are added, while BBH and abliterated-model general-capability entries are removed. X-Teaming scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same game formulation, safe-refusal assumption, Nash-equilibrium theorem and contradiction proof. The reward and optimization equations are mathematically unchanged; revised notation and pseudocode add no new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain online self-play safety training, greater attack diversity and a conditional safety guarantee. v3 refocuses headline empirical claims on improving already aligned models across four scales and 12 safety evaluations, replacing the earlier numerical examples. Broader model generalizability was already claimed provisionally in v2 Appendix A.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of computational efficiency, perplexity as evidence of novel attacks, and architecture sensitivity of safeguarding alternatives. Section 6 distinguishes modest CoT compliance benefits in Qwen from larger benefits in Llama. The earlier single-model-family limitation is removed; most other limitations and safeguard arguments are retained.

D1.justification: The execution description changes from four A100s plus four L40s and 10–15 hours to four H200s with co-location/offloading and 2–4 hours. v3 newly identifies the X-Teaming planner/judge, Qwen2.5-32B attacker and TextGrad procedure. Conversely, v2's explicit 100-prompt holdout and ten-step evaluation cadence are no longer documented. The code-access destination is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds targeted contrasts with adversarial-training work by Xhonneux, Howe and Jain, and Appendix D.2 positions the method against LLM-LAT and CircuitBreaker. Several earlier jailbreak and abliteration references are removed. The central positioning as fully online, full-parameter MARL for safety remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and results narrative are substantially rewritten. Research-question subsections become takeaway-based discussion; training details move into Appendix A, additional results are reorganized into Appendix D, and limitations move to Appendix E. Broader-impact material becomes an ethics statement, and a reproducibility statement is added.

P2.justification: The main tables are redesigned around five model pairs with percentage-change rows and a Qwen14B ablation. New capability, safeguarding, runtime and novelty tables expand the displays. Figure 3 is redrawn with changed axes and holdout-diversity panels; the separate earlier holdout figure disappears, and bootstrap plots move to the appendix. Typography and page layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessment of practical value through external safeguarding comparisons, broader capability checks, computational measurements and clearer multi-turn implementation details. The gain is limited by removed BBH and holdout documentation, plus unreconciled table values: the abliterated baseline's AlpacaEval score is 19.70 in Table 1 but 19.22 in Table 7. Since broad model and multi-turn evidence already existed in v2 Appendix A, the overall improvement is useful but limited.
